newsitem.title: JAPAN: Joining EMU not crucial for UK economy -- Clarke.
newsitem.headline: Joining EMU not crucial for UK economy -- Clarke.

text.p: British finance minister Kenneth Clarke said on Friday that Britain's participation or non-participation in a European single currency was not crucial to the success of the British economy.
Clarke, speaking to British business leaders in Tokyo, said:
"I don't think our participation or non-participation is crucial to our future success or threatens us in any way.
"I don't think staying out of the EMU poses any threat to the predominant position of the City of London," he said.
Clarke said that if he was French or German he would want Britain to join the European Monetary Union since Britain would be a desirable partner from their perspective.
However, he reiterated Britain's stance that it would reserve the option of joining the EMU and base its judgement on whether it would serve the country's economic interests.

"What the British have to do is to decide whether membership of EMU would or would not add strength to our economy as we seek to continue to succeed in the European Union and in the bigger global economy," he said.
